question: True or false: the well-tempered of Bach's title means the equal temperament pianos use today?
answer: False. In Bach's day well-tempered meant any tuning in which all 24 keys were usable, and most such tunings left the keys unequal, so C major and F sharp major had different colours. Equal temperament, every semitone the same size, was one option and became the norm on pianos only in the 19th century.
move: Read an old word in its own century before reading it in ours.
trap: Reading the modern meaning of a tuning word back into 1722.
source: Duffin, How Equal Temperament Ruined Harmony, 2007
reference: Duffin, How Equal Temperament Ruined Harmony (and Why You Should Care), W. W. Norton, 2007
